title: FactLedger Step 0: Documents, Units, Pieces
subtitle: 19,436 documents split into 44,262 units, with a per-piece speaker table
description:
Every document in the IT 494 memory-backend corpus, split into units, with a piece table that says what each stretch of a file is and who is speaking there. 19,436 documents, 44,262 units, 227,100 pieces, produced in one pass by a public notebook for $7.72.

This is the input to a memory backend, not a finished analysis. Step 0 answers one question about a raw file: where does this document divide, and what kind of text is each part? No entities, no facts, no summaries.

**Not a chunker.** Nothing is cut on length. A language model reads a numbered list of the file's own lines and says where the front matter ends, where the body begins, where the notes and references and appendix are, and where each chapter or scene or turn starts. Units group those natural parts up to a size cap, cutting only at boundaries the model named and copied back so the copy could be checked against the line.

Two properties, verified on all 19,436 documents rather than asserted:

- Pieces and units tile the document. Every byte belongs to exactly one piece and exactly one unit, no gaps, no overlaps.
- A unit never mixes kinds. It is all body, or all references, or all appendix, never running from the end of a chapter into the footnotes.

The piece table carries the speaker, so a quote's voice is the author of the piece holding it.

**Files.** `documents.jsonl` (19,436 rows: identity, title, author, date, full text), `units.jsonl` (44,262 rows: character ranges into that text), `pieces.jsonl` (227,100 rows: what each stretch is and who speaks), `papers.jsonl` (141 withheld papers with a URL and a hash), `receipt.json` (the run's own counts). `README.md`, `SCHEMA.md`, `METHOD.md`, `PROVENANCE.md` and `LIMITS.md` are in the dataset.

**Corpus.** 19,206 LongMemEval-S sessions, 31 volumes of Greek and Roman literature including six OCR'd institutional scans, 29 Oz books, 20 GraphRAG-Bench novels, 9 Sherlock Holmes volumes, and 141 reference papers. Three shapes on purpose: clean e-texts, damaged scans with heavy apparatus, and assistant chat logs.

**Reference papers have no text.** Their publishers' licenses mostly forbid redistribution, so those 141 rows carry a null text and the flag `text withheld: license`; their units and pieces are here in full, and `papers.jsonl` gives the source URL and the PDF's sha256 so the text can be rebuilt with the same notebook.

**Licensing is layered.** Packaging, schema and every derived field are MIT. The literature is public domain in the United States by expiry of term. GraphRAG-Bench and LongMemEval are MIT and keep their own notices. See PROVENANCE.md.

**Known limits are documented, not hidden.** 72 documents carry a substantive flag; 79 pointers out of 370 mismatches could not be recovered and those breaks were dropped; 6 units are over the cap; 52 documents carry no date because the run never infers one. LIMITS.md gives the counts and the diagnosis.

Made by https://www.kaggle.com/code/jhffmn/factledger-extractor (factledger-extractor 1.5, gpt-5.6-luna). Raw inputs: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jhffmn/it494-narrative-corpora-raw

IT 494 directed project, Illinois State University, fall 2026.
userSpecifiedSources:
SOURCES. Project Gutenberg (29 Oz volumes, 9 Sherlock Holmes volumes, 25 volumes of Greek and Roman literature); Archive.org institutional scans (6 OCR'd Loeb and 19th-century volumes); GraphRAG-Bench novel contexts, MIT, https://github.com/GraphRAG-Bench/GraphRAG-Benchmark; LongMemEval-S sessions, MIT, https://github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval; and 141 reference papers fetched from arXiv, the ACL Anthology and publisher sites.

COLLECTION. Every file was fetched by an idempotent, title-verifying script that records the source URL, byte count and sha256 per file. The raw inputs are published byte-identical, with those manifests, at https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jhffmn/it494-narrative-corpora-raw . The two benchmark corpora were unpacked from their upstream JSON into one file per document; nothing was cleaned, normalised or truncated.

PROCESSING. One pass of the public notebook https://www.kaggle.com/code/jhffmn/factledger-extractor (factledger-extractor 1.5, gpt-5.6-luna) over 19,437 files on 2026-09-06. The extractor sees a raw file and nothing else: no filename convention and no per-corpus rule. Each document is shown to the model as its own numbered lines; the model points at a line by number and copies that line's text, and a boundary is kept only when the copy verifies against the line it names. Units group the resulting pieces up to a 4,000-word cap, cutting only at boundaries the model named. Verified on all 19,436 exported documents: pieces and units tile every document with no gaps or overlaps, unit ids are unique, positions are dense, and no unit mixes a region kind. Total cost $7.72, median $0.013 per document. METHOD.md gives the full procedure.

LICENSING. Packaging, schema and every derived field are MIT. The literature is public domain in the United States by expiry of term. GraphRAG-Bench and LongMemEval are MIT and keep their own notices. The 141 reference papers are withheld: their document rows carry a null text and the flag 'text withheld: license', while their units and pieces are complete, and papers.jsonl gives each one's source URL and PDF sha256 so the text can be rebuilt with block 1 of the same notebook. PROVENANCE.md gives this per corpus.

KNOWN LIMITS. 72 documents carry a substantive flag; 79 of 370 pointer mismatches could not be recovered and those breaks were dropped; 6 units exceed the word cap; 52 documents carry no date because the run never infers one. LIMITS.md gives the counts and the diagnosis. This is not ground truth: there is no gold segmentation for these works, and what is verified is internal consistency plus the pointer gate.

PART OF the IT 494 directed project, Illinois State University, fall 2026.
